sentences.en: Hey there, Shankar here.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是 Shankar。

sentences.en: Since we first published this episode
sentences.zh: 自我们首次发布这期节目以来，

sentences.en: with Francesca Gino in 2018,
sentences.zh: 也就是 2018 年 Francesca Gino 的那期，

sentences.en: other researchers have raised concerns
sentences.zh: 其他研究人员对她工作的完整性

sentences.en: about the integrity of her work.
sentences.zh: 提出了质疑。

sentences.en: In 2023, a group of scientists publicly alleged
sentences.zh: 2023 年，一群科学家公开指控

sentences.en: that she had fabricated data in some of her studies.
sentences.zh: 她在部分研究中伪造了数据。

sentences.en: You can find more information about their analysis
sentences.zh: 你们可以在 datacollada.org

sentences.en: at datacollada.org.
sentences.zh: 找到关于他们分析的更多信息。

sentences.en: Francesca Gino has denied the allegations.
sentences.zh: Francesca Gino 否认了这些指控。

sentences.en: A number of her studies have been retracted
sentences.zh: 她的一些研究已经被发表这些研究的期刊

sentences.en: by the journals that published them,
sentences.zh: 撤稿了，

sentences.en: including a study about karaoke that is referenced in this episode.
sentences.zh: 其中包括本期节目中提到的关于卡拉 OK 的研究。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《Hidden Brain》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是 Shankar Vedantam。

sentences.en: Every day, listeners reach out to us,
sentences.zh: 每天都有听众联系我们，

sentences.en: asking for research that will help them solve the problems we all face in life.
sentences.zh: 寻求能帮助他们解决生活中所面临问题的研究。

sentences.en: Last summer, we decided to put out a series that would speak to these concerns,
sentences.zh: 去年夏天，我们决定推出一个系列节目来回应这些关切，

sentences.en: highlighting stories about the decisions we make from the mundane to the momentous.
sentences.zh: 重点讲述关于我们所做决策的故事，从琐事到大事。

sentences.en: We call the series U 2.0,
sentences.zh: 我们将这个系列称为“U 2.0”，

sentences.en: And it was so popular, we decided to bring it back this year.
sentences.zh: 它非常受欢迎，所以我们决定今年把它带回来。

sentences.en: It's six weeks of advice about things like jobs.
sentences.zh: 这是为期六周的建议，涵盖工作等方面。

sentences.en: People for whom the work is a calling tend to be better performers
sentences.zh: 那些将工作视为使命的人往往表现更好，

sentences.en: and be far more deeply engaged in it, regardless of what the work is.
sentences.zh: 而且无论工作内容是什么，他们投入的程度都要深得多。

sentences.en: Relationships.
sentences.zh: 人际关系。

sentences.en: We look to our partners to be our sculptors,
sentences.zh: 我们期待伴侣成为我们的雕塑家，

sentences.en: to help us until we actually grow toward the best ideal version of ourselves.
sentences.zh: 帮助我们成长，直到我们真正成为理想中最好的自己。

sentences.en: And behavior that we all struggle to change.
sentences.zh: 以及我们都在努力改变的行为。

sentences.en: We'll kick the series off today in a bookstore.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将从一家书店开启这个系列。

sentences.en: A few years ago, social scientist Francesca Gino was browsing the shelves when she came across an unusual-looking book in the cooking section.
sentences.zh: 几年前，社会科学家 Francesca Gino 在逛书店时，在烹饪区偶然发现了一本看起来很不寻常的书。

sentences.en: This recipe book, they look a little bit different, and the title said, Never Trust a Skinny Italian Chef.
sentences.zh: 这本食谱书看起来有点不同，书名是《永远别相信一个瘦削的意大利厨师》。

sentences.en: And being Italian, I was very intrigued.
sentences.zh: 身为意大利人，我非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And as I flipped through the pages, it became clear that this was not your typical recipe book.
sentences.zh: 当我翻阅书页时，很明显这不是一本普通的食谱书。

sentences.en: The dishes were playful, quirky, improbable.
sentences.zh: 这些菜肴既俏皮、古怪，又令人难以置信。

sentences.en: Snails were paired with coffee sauce,
sentences.zh: 蜗牛配咖啡酱，

sentences.en: veal tongue with charcoal powder.
sentences.zh: 小牛舌配木炭粉。

sentences.en: The recipes had titles like
sentences.zh: 食谱的标题有诸如

sentences.en: How to Burn a Sardine.
sentences.zh: 《如何烧焦沙丁鱼》。

sentences.en: And, oops, I dropped the lemon tart.
sentences.zh: 还有，《哎呀，我把柠檬塔掉地上了》。

sentences.en: There were pictures of beautiful dishes.
sentences.zh: 书里有精美菜肴的图片。

sentences.en: Who could resist a dish called
sentences.zh: 谁能抵挡得住一道名为

sentences.en: the crunchy part of the lasagna?
sentences.zh: “千层面脆皮”的菜呢？

sentences.en: Now, if you know anything about Italians,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你对意大利人有所了解，

sentences.en: First of all, we have lots of rules when it comes to cooking.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们在烹饪方面有很多规矩。

sentences.en: And second, we really cherish our traditional dishes,
sentences.zh: 其次，我们非常珍视传统菜肴，

sentences.en: especially because they've been passed on for generations.
sentences.zh: 尤其是因为它们代代相传。

sentences.en: But this chef, one of the most successful in the world,
sentences.zh: 但这位厨师，作为世界上最成功的厨师之一，

sentences.en: couldn't resist circling back to one big existential question.
sentences.zh: 却忍不住回过头来思考一个重大的存在主义问题。

sentences.en: Why is it that we cook the dish in this way?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们要用这种方式烹饪这道菜？

sentences.en: Why is it that we cook the dish in this way?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们要用这种方式烹饪这道菜？

sentences.en: It's the kind of question Francesca loved.
sentences.zh: 这正是 Francesca 喜欢的那种问题。

sentences.en: As a professor at Harvard Business School, she has spent most of her career studying non-conformists,
sentences.zh: 作为哈佛商学院的教授，她职业生涯的大部分时间都在研究非传统者，

sentences.en: specifically people who break the rules and end up in trouble.
sentences.zh: 特别是那些打破常规并最终惹上麻烦的人。

sentences.en: But now, standing at the bookstore, she wondered, when can defying norms lead to innovation?
sentences.zh: 但现在，站在书店里，她想知道，挑战规范何时能带来创新？

sentences.en: Can letting go of tradition lead to the most sublime examples of creative thinking?
sentences.zh: 抛弃传统能否带来最崇高的创造性思维范例？

sentences.en: To find out, she got in touch with the man behind the cookbook,
sentences.zh: 为了找到答案，她联系了这本食谱背后的那个人，

sentences.en: the so-called Jimi Hendrix of Italian cooking, Massimo Bottura.
sentences.zh: 也就是所谓的意大利烹饪界的吉米·亨德里克斯（Jimi Hendrix），Massimo Bottura。

sentences.en: After a few conversations, you said,
sentences.zh: 经过几次交谈，你说，

sentences.en: look, if you really want to understand the business, you've got to come to Modena.
sentences.zh: 听着，如果你真的想了解这个行业，你必须来摩德纳。

sentences.en: And I was like, of course, why say no to an invitation to a three Michelin star restaurant?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，当然，谁会拒绝米其林三星餐厅的邀请呢？

sentences.en: I'm on my way.
sentences.zh: 我已经在路上了。

sentences.en: This week, we'll follow Francesca on her mission to understand the minds of successful nonconformists.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们将跟随 Francesca 的脚步，去了解成功非传统者的思想。

sentences.en: Her book about this quest is called Rebel Talent,
sentences.zh: 她关于这次探索的书名为《叛逆天赋》（Rebel Talent），

sentences.en: why it pays to break the rules at work and in life.
sentences.zh: 讲述了为什么在工作和生活中打破常规是有益的。

sentences.en: I think we really need to shift our thinking.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们真的需要转变思维方式。

sentences.en: Rebels are not troublemakers.
sentences.zh: 叛逆者不是捣乱分子。

sentences.en: They're not outcasts.
sentences.zh: 他们也不是被排斥的人。

sentences.en: Rebels are people who break rules that should be broken.
sentences.zh: 叛逆者是那些打破应该被打破的规则的人。

sentences.en: They break rules that hold them and others back.
sentences.zh: 他们打破了束缚自己和他人的规则。

sentences.en: And their way of rule-breaking is constructive rather than destructive.
sentences.zh: 而且他们打破规则的方式是建设性的，而不是破坏性的。

sentences.en: It creates positive change.
sentences.zh: 它创造了积极的改变。

sentences.en: How to be a rebel, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 如何成为一名叛逆者，本周《Hidden Brain》为您呈现。

sentences.en: So I showed up at the restaurant for my first day with my notebook, and basically I was given
sentences.zh: 所以我带着笔记本出现在餐厅的第一天，基本上我被发给了

sentences.en: an apron.
sentences.zh: 一件围裙。

sentences.en: For the entire day, I was put to work in the front of the house as a server.
sentences.zh: 整整一天，我都被安排在前厅做服务员。

sentences.en: And again,
sentences.zh: 再说一次，

sentences.en: it was an amazing experience because I had no qualification.
sentences.zh: 这是一次很棒的经历，因为我没有任何资格。

sentences.en: I clearly didn't know what I was
sentences.zh: 我显然不知道自己在

sentences.en: doing.
sentences.zh: 做什么。

sentences.en: I made a lot of mistakes, but that was just an example of doing things a little bit
sentences.zh: 我犯了很多错误，但这只是以稍微不同的方式

sentences.en: differently.
sentences.zh: 做事的一个例子。

sentences.en: So of course, if you're a smart chef, the one thing you don't do is bring an
sentences.zh: 所以当然，如果你是一个聪明的厨师，你绝对不会做的一件事就是带一个

sentences.en: amateur into your three Michelin star restaurant and ask her to start serving the dishes.
sentences.zh: 业余爱好者进入你的米其林三星餐厅，并让她开始上菜。

sentences.en: I can
sentences.zh: 我能

sentences.en: just imagine all the ways that that could go wrong.
sentences.zh: 想象出所有可能出错的地方。

sentences.en: Did it?
sentences.zh: 真的出错了吗？

sentences.en: That is exactly what was going through my
sentences.zh: 这正是我在犯错时脑子里想的，

sentences.en: head as I was making mistakes from putting the very carefully arranged dishes down onto the table
sentences.zh: 从把精心摆盘的菜肴放到桌上开始，

sentences.en: that are very specific ways in which the dish gets arranged so that you get the right anticipation
sentences.zh: 菜肴的摆放方式非常讲究，这样你才能在吃的时候

sentences.en: of what the dish is going to be about as you eat it.
sentences.zh: 对这道菜的味道有正确的期待。

sentences.en: And throughout the day, the team members were working with me
sentences.zh: 整整一天，和我一起在前厅工作的团队成员

sentences.en: in the front of the house, were just helping me.
sentences.zh: 都在帮助我。

sentences.en: And when I was making mistakes, they were very subtly trying to correct.
sentences.zh: 当我犯错时，他们会非常含蓄地试图纠正。

sentences.en: So they were adjusting the plate, or if I brought to a table
sentences.zh: 所以他们会调整盘子，或者如果我拿错了餐具到桌上，

sentences.en: the wrong utensils, they would show up and somehow bring another set
sentences.zh: 他们会出现，并以某种方式拿来另一套

sentences.en: that was the rice set for the type of dish that was being served.
sentences.zh: 适合所上菜肴的餐具。

sentences.en: So I understand that if I were to visit the restaurant,
sentences.zh: 所以我了解到，如果我去那家餐厅，

sentences.en: I might sometimes see Massimo Bottura outside unloading produce from the trucks
sentences.zh: 我有时可能会看到 Massimo Bottura 在外面从卡车上卸下农产品，

sentences.en: or sweeping the pavement.
sentences.zh: 或者在扫地。

sentences.en: He doesn't seem like someone who stands on airs.
sentences.zh: 他看起来不像是一个摆架子的人。

sentences.en: He's very much into the trenches.
sentences.zh: 他非常深入一线。

sentences.en: One of the first things that he does when he shows up at the restaurant in the morning
sentences.zh: 他早上到餐厅时做的第一件事之一

sentences.en: is to put his white chef's coat on,
sentences.zh: 就是穿上他白色的厨师服，

sentences.en: and then he does go outside with a broom and sweep the streets.
sentences.zh: 然后他真的会拿着扫帚到外面去扫街。

sentences.en: And you're there looking at him and the sous chef and the people working in the restaurants are there looking at him and you ask the question, why is it that he's doing that?
sentences.zh: 你站在那里看着他，副主厨和在餐厅工作的人也在看着他，你会问，他为什么要那样做？

sentences.en: But the second question that you ask yourself is, why is it that I'm not doing it?
sentences.zh: 但你问自己的第二个问题是，为什么我不那样做呢？

sentences.en: And so you're feeling motivated to take on roles and activities that are roles that are not scripted because of where you sit or where you work in the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 所以你会感到有动力去承担一些角色和活动，这些角色不是因为你在餐厅的位置或工作地点而预先设定的。

sentences.en: It's very refreshing.
sentences.zh: 这非常令人耳目一新。

sentences.en: And, of course, he actually tries to bring this approach to the food that he is making as well.
sentences.zh: 当然，他实际上也试图将这种方法应用到他制作的食物中。

sentences.en: I want you to listen to this clip of music because you say the chef actually asked his staff to build a dish based on this song.
sentences.zh: 我想让你听听这段音乐，因为你说这位厨师实际上要求他的员工根据这首歌创作一道菜。

sentences.en: Holly came from Miami, F.L.A.
sentences.zh: Holly 来自佛罗里达州的迈阿密，

sentences.en: Hitchhiked away across the U.S.A.
sentences.zh: 搭便车横穿美国，

sentences.en: Plucked her eyebrows on the way.
sentences.zh: 路上拔了眉毛，

sentences.en: Shaved her legs and then he was a she.
sentences.zh: 刮了腿毛，然后他变成了她。

sentences.en: She says, hey, babe, take a walk on the wild side.
sentences.zh: 她说，嘿，宝贝，去狂野的一面走走吧。

sentences.en: Said, hey, honey, take a walk on the wild side.
sentences.zh: 说，嘿，亲爱的，去狂野的一面走走吧。

sentences.en: So what was going on, Francesca?
sentences.zh: 那么当时发生了什么，Francesca？

sentences.en: How do you make a dish based on a song?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能根据一首歌做出一道菜呢？

sentences.en: It was one of the many ways that Massimo Bottura inspires the people working in the kitchen
sentences.zh: 这是 Massimo Bottura 激励厨房工作人员的众多方式之一，

sentences.en: and really asks them to bring out their own contribution and their own voices.
sentences.zh: 他真的要求他们展现出自己的贡献和自己的声音。

sentences.en: So you would see him walk into the kitchen and say,
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到他走进厨房说，

sentences.en: Lou Reed, walk to the outside.
sentences.zh: 卢·里德，走到户外。

sentences.en: or a different name of a song or a different poem
sentences.zh: 或者一首不同歌曲的名字，或者一首不同的诗，

sentences.en: or the name of a phrase of something that he was reading recently
sentences.zh: 或者他最近读到的某个短语，

sentences.en: or the name of a piece of art that he saw at an art show.
sentences.zh: 或者他在艺术展上看到的一件艺术品的名字。

sentences.en: And what he's trying to do is asking people to think about how that song
sentences.zh: 他试图做的是要求人们思考那首歌

sentences.en: or how that piece of art inspired them to come up with their own dish.
sentences.zh: 或那件艺术品是如何激励他们想出自己的菜肴的。

sentences.en: And what he's trying to do at the very core
sentences.zh: 他核心想要做的是

sentences.en: is making sure that people don't show up at work
sentences.zh: 确保人们在工作时不会

sentences.en: and somehow they leave their identity at the door,
sentences.zh: 把自己的身份留在门外，

sentences.en: but rather they show up and they're being who they are.
sentences.zh: 而是展现真实的自我。

sentences.en: They're bringing their ideas forward, their contributions forward,
sentences.zh: 他们提出自己的想法，做出自己的贡献，

sentences.en: independent of their background, their nationalities,
sentences.zh: 无论他们的背景、国籍如何，

sentences.en: or how much training they have.
sentences.zh: 或者他们受过多少培训。

sentences.en: And when you spoke to the staff at the restaurant,
sentences.zh: 当你和餐厅的员工交谈时，

sentences.en: what did they say the role of the chef was in inspiring them?
sentences.zh: 他们说厨师在激励他们方面扮演了什么角色？

sentences.en: Did they actually agree that these techniques were actually bringing out the best in them?
sentences.zh: 他们是否真的同意这些技巧确实激发了他们最好的一面？

sentences.en: What the staff said, which is really interesting, is that Massimo is the type of leader who never says hi, hi, hi, hi.
sentences.zh: 员工们说的话非常有趣，他们说 Massimo 是那种从不说“我、我、我”的领导者。

sentences.en: It's always about the we.
sentences.zh: 他总是谈论“我们”。

sentences.en: He describes the restaurant as a crew or as a ship.
sentences.zh: 他把餐厅描述为一个团队或一艘船。

sentences.en: In fact, he often talks about being on a pirate ship.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他经常谈论在海盗船上工作。

sentences.en: And sometimes the waters out there are going to be turbulent.
sentences.zh: 有时外面的海域会波涛汹涌。

sentences.en: But for the very fact that we are going to bring out our individual contributions, but we're going to do so being aware that we are part of a team,
sentences.zh: 但正因为我们要贡献出个人的力量，同时意识到我们是团队的一部分，

sentences.en: no matter how terrible in the sea is, we're going to succeed.
sentences.zh: 无论大海多么可怕，我们都会成功。

sentences.en: And people do feel very inspired by the way he leads the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 人们确实被他领导餐厅的方式深深激励了。

sentences.en: Here's another thing that makes Massimo a rebel.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事让 Massimo 成为一名叛逆者。

sentences.en: He asks a lot of questions about why things are the way they are.
sentences.zh: 他会问很多关于事物为何如此的问题。

sentences.en: For Francesca, a fearless curiosity is at the heart of rebel talent.
sentences.zh: 对于 Francesca 来说，无畏的好奇心是叛逆天赋的核心。

sentences.en: Bottura opened up a restaurant by asking the question, why not?
sentences.zh: Bottura 开餐厅时问的问题是：为什么不呢？

sentences.en: He had no experience in running a restaurant, let alone cooking, because he didn't go to culinary school.
sentences.zh: 他没有任何经营餐厅的经验，更不用说烹饪了，因为他没有上过烹饪学校。

sentences.en: He was in law school.
sentences.zh: 他曾就读于法学院。

sentences.en: He was there for two years as a way to stick to what his father wanted.
sentences.zh: 他在那里待了两年，只是为了坚持他父亲的意愿。

sentences.en: and then he didn't enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 后来他发现自己并不喜欢。

sentences.en: And when his brother, one of these brothers told him about this restaurant
sentences.zh: 当他的兄弟，也就是其中一位兄弟告诉他这家餐厅

sentences.en: that was up for sale, he really asked himself the question, why not?
sentences.zh: 正在出售时，他真的问了自己一个问题：为什么不呢？

sentences.en: That's curiosity.
sentences.zh: 这就是好奇心。

sentences.en: We are so often focused on efficiency and getting things done.
sentences.zh: 我们太过于关注效率和完成任务了。

sentences.en: We have a very long to-do liSt.
sentences.zh: 我们有一份很长的待办事项清单。

sentences.en: But what that often comes at the cost of is allowing us to explore
sentences.zh: 但这往往是以牺牲我们探索的能力为代价的，

sentences.en: the way we used to when we were a very little kid.
sentences.zh: 就像我们小时候那样。

sentences.en: And that came very naturally to us.
sentences.zh: 那对我们来说是很自然的事情。

sentences.en: So I see too many leaders who focus so much on efficiency that curiosity shut down in people.
sentences.zh: 所以我看到太多的领导者过于关注效率，以至于人们的好奇心都被扼杀了。

sentences.en: And that's too bad because curiosity leads to all sorts of great results and great outcomes.
sentences.zh: 这很可惜，因为好奇心能带来各种伟大的成果和结果。

sentences.en: There's a tension that runs through much of the book.
sentences.zh: 书中贯穿着一种张力。

sentences.en: And the tension is the tension between expertise and experimentation.
sentences.zh: 这种张力就是专业知识与实验探索之间的张力。

sentences.en: And I want to come back and talk about this over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我想反复回到这一点来讨论。

sentences.en: But I also want to do it through the lens of another story that you explore.
sentences.zh: 但我也想通过你探讨的另一个故事的视角来谈谈。

sentences.en: you've looked at the story of Captain Chesley Sullenberger,
sentences.zh: 你研究了切斯利·萨伦伯格机长的故事，

sentences.en: better known as Captain Sully.
sentences.zh: 也就是大家熟知的萨利机长。

sentences.en: He was at the controls of U.S.
sentences.zh: 他当时是全美航空

sentences.en: Airways Flight 1549.
sentences.zh: 1549号航班的机长。

sentences.en: The plane had just taken off from LaGuardia Airport in New York.
sentences.zh: 飞机刚从纽约拉瓜迪亚机场起飞。

sentences.en: A flock of birds flies into the plane.
sentences.zh: 一群鸟撞进了飞机。

sentences.en: I want to play you a bit of tape from the cockpit recorder.
sentences.zh: 我想给你们放一段驾驶舱录音。

sentences.en: Captain Sully radios air traffic controllers in New York
sentences.zh: 萨利机长通过无线电联系纽约的空中交通管制员，

sentences.en: using the call sign Cactus 1539.
sentences.zh: 呼号是“仙人掌1539”。

sentences.en: The plane is descending at a terrifying rate.
sentences.zh: 飞机正在以惊人的速度下降。

sentences.en: The controllers try to figure out what to do.
sentences.zh: 管制员们试图弄清楚该怎么办。

sentences.en: Tower, stop you to park.
sentences.zh: 塔台，停止起飞。

sentences.en: He's got an emergency returning.
sentences.zh: 他有紧急情况，要返航。

sentences.en: Who is it?
sentences.zh: 是谁？

sentences.en: He, uh, bird strike.
sentences.zh: 他，呃，遭遇鸟击。

sentences.en: He lost all engines.
sentences.zh: 他失去了所有引擎。

sentences.en: He lost the thrust in the engines.
sentences.zh: 引擎失去了推力。

sentences.en: He's returning immediately.
sentences.zh: 他正在立即返航。

sentences.en: Captain 1529, which engines?
sentences.zh: 1529机长，哪个引擎？

sentences.en: He lost thrust in both engines, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说两个引擎都失去了推力。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 收到。

sentences.en: Captain Sully asks for landing options, but he quickly decides none of them will work.
sentences.zh: 萨利机长询问降落方案，但他很快断定这些方案都行不通。

sentences.en: Captain 1529, turn right 2-8-0.
sentences.zh: 1529机长，右转航向280。

sentences.en: And then, landing a plane in the Hudson River.
sentences.zh: 然后，飞机降落在哈德逊河上。

sentences.en: Francesca, you described this incident as a striking example of rebel talent.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯卡，你将这次事件描述为“反叛者天赋”的一个显著例子。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: If you think about the situation that Captain Sully was under,
sentences.zh: 如果你设身处地去想萨利机长当时所处的境地，

sentences.en: most of us would go to the obvious answer.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人都会选择显而易见的答案。

sentences.en: We are under a lot of pressure.
sentences.zh: 我们承受着巨大的压力。

sentences.en: We have no time.
sentences.zh: 我们没有时间。

sentences.en: We are really stressed.
sentences.zh: 我们压力很大。

sentences.en: And what our mind would do very naturally is to narrow our way of thinking.
sentences.zh: 而我们的大脑很自然地会收窄我们的思维方式。

sentences.en: But if you read the accident reports or if you were to talk to Sally, you would understand that what he did instead was to consider options.
sentences.zh: 但如果你读过事故报告，或者和萨利谈过，你就会明白，他所做的是考虑各种选择。

sentences.en: He kept asking himself what it is that I could be doing.
sentences.zh: 他不断问自己：我还能做些什么？

sentences.en: And in a place where most people would close their mind, he kept his mind open.
sentences.zh: 在大多数人会封闭思维的地方，他保持了开放的心态。

sentences.en: Rather than going to the obvious answer of landing to the nearest airport, he thought creatively about the problem and came up with this idea of landing in the Hudson River.
sentences.zh: 他没有选择降落到最近机场这一显而易见的答案，而是创造性地思考问题，并想出了降落在哈德逊河上的主意。

sentences.en: So that's what rebels are all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是“反叛者”的特质。

sentences.en: People who rather than just following the script or just following what they've learned in their training, they stay open minded.
sentences.zh: 他们不是只会照本宣科或遵循训练中学到的东西，而是保持开放的心态。

sentences.en: They look at the problem from a very different perspective, no matter how much time they have to think about it, and then they creatively solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 无论有多少时间思考，他们都会从完全不同的角度审视问题，然后创造性地解决问题。

sentences.en: Captain Sully had 208 seconds by the time he discovered that he had no thrust in the engine and the time he ditched the plane in the Hudson River.
sentences.zh: 从萨利机长发现引擎失去推力，到他将飞机迫降在哈德逊河上，他只有208秒的时间。

sentences.en: That's true rebel talent.
sentences.zh: 那才是真正的反叛者天赋。

sentences.en: One of the things, again, the story reveals to me is this tension between expertise and experimentation.
sentences.zh: 这个故事再次向我揭示了专业知识与实验探索之间的这种张力。

sentences.en: So if you have expertise, but you're not willing to experiment, you become predictable, you become boring.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你有专业知识，却不愿意去实验，你就会变得可预测，变得无趣。

sentences.en: But if you experiment without having expertise, you know, that can be amateurish.
sentences.zh: 但如果你没有专业知识就去实验，那可能会显得很业余。

sentences.en: If you ask me to land a plane in the Hudson River, it's going to end in disaster.
sentences.zh: 如果你让我把飞机降落在哈德逊河上，那只会是一场灾难。

sentences.en: So there's something that happens when you combine expertise with experimentation.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你把专业知识与实验探索结合起来时，会发生一些奇妙的事情。

sentences.en: That's where the magic is.
sentences.zh: 那才是魔力所在。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: One of the things that many people might not know about Captain Sully that I learned when I had the opportunity to interview him,
sentences.zh: 关于萨利机长，很多人可能不知道的一点是，我在采访他时了解到，

sentences.en: is that by the time the accident happened, he had experience flying all sorts of planes.
sentences.zh: 在事故发生时，他已经拥有驾驶各种飞机的经验。

sentences.en: He also served as a volunteer in teams that look at prior accidents and try to understand what it is that happened.
sentences.zh: 他还曾作为志愿者参与过调查过往事故的团队，试图了解事故发生的原因。

sentences.en: So he had so much experience once he was in that dire situation.
sentences.zh: 所以，当他处于那种危急时刻时，他拥有极其丰富的经验。

sentences.en: And yet, one of the things that is true about him is that every time he walked on a plane,
sentences.zh: 然而，关于他的一点是，每次他登上飞机时，

sentences.en: He asked himself the question, what it is that I could learn?
sentences.zh: 他都会问自己：我能学到什么？

sentences.en: How is it that this could be different?
sentences.zh: 这有什么不同之处？

sentences.en: He had that type of intellectual humility that kept him open-minded,
sentences.zh: 他拥有那种保持开放心态的智识谦逊，

sentences.en: despite the fact that he was accumulating throughout his career a lot of experience.
sentences.zh: 尽管他在职业生涯中积累了大量的经验。

sentences.en: That's what often we miss out on.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们经常错失的东西。

sentences.en: We gain experience, and by gaining experience and knowledge,
sentences.zh: 我们获得了经验，通过积累经验和知识，

sentences.en: we believe that we all have the right answer.
sentences.zh: 我们认为自己掌握了正确的答案。

sentences.en: And we don't stay humble.
sentences.zh: 我们不再保持谦逊。

sentences.en: We don't have that type of intellectual humility that keep us focused on what's left to learn
sentences.zh: 我们没有那种让我们专注于“还有什么需要学习”的智识谦逊，

sentences.en: rather than what it is that we know already.
sentences.zh: 而不是专注于“我们已经知道了什么”。

sentences.en: Captain Sully and Massimo Bottura tried daring things and achieved extraordinary results.
sentences.zh: 萨利机长和马西莫·博图拉都尝试过大胆的事情，并取得了非凡的成就。

sentences.en: It's easy to admire them, but why is it so hard to be like them?
sentences.zh: 钦佩他们很容易，但为什么像他们一样却那么难？

sentences.en: It turns out a curious psychological roadblock often gets in the way.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，一种好奇心方面的心理障碍往往会阻碍我们。

sentences.en: We're talking about successful rebels.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是成功的反叛者。

sentences.en: people who defy the status quo and produce creative breakthroughs.
sentences.zh: 那些挑战现状并创造出突破性成果的人。

sentences.en: We've seen how this worked with Captain Sully and Chef Bottura.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到了萨利机长和博图拉主厨是如何做到这一点的。

sentences.en: So why are people like this so rare?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么这样的人如此罕见？

sentences.en: Why do so many of us find it hard to channel our inner Bottura?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们许多人觉得很难激发内在的“博图拉”？

sentences.en: You might think the problem is we're not experts.
sentences.zh: 你可能认为问题在于我们不是专家。

sentences.en: We're not skilled chefs or great pilots.
sentences.zh: 我们不是技术精湛的厨师或伟大的飞行员。

sentences.en: But in fact, the problem is often the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，问题往往恰恰相反。

sentences.en: We know too much.
sentences.zh: 我们知道得太多了。

sentences.en: My colleagues and I were fascinated by this idea that experience could be costly because in a lot of our classes,
sentences.zh: 我和同事们对“经验可能是有代价的”这一观点很着迷，因为在我们的许多课堂上，

sentences.en: we're actually there telling our students that they should gain knowledge, that the information is power, that experience is important.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上是在告诉学生，他们应该获取知识，信息就是力量，经验很重要。

sentences.en: And so we explored this in a data set of millions of data points on how cardiologists behave in their surgery when they do open-heart surgeries.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在一个包含数百万数据点的数据集中探讨了这个问题，研究心脏病专家在进行心脏直视手术时的行为。

sentences.en: And what was interesting is that we could explore what happened to this cardiologist and their behavior after the Food and Drug Administration put out an announcement that,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我们可以探索在食品药品监督管理局发布公告后，这些心脏病专家的行为发生了什么变化，

sentences.en: if I were to simplify, basically told them that the way they were using the technology in their surgery was not good for patients.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，公告告诉他们，他们在手术中使用该技术的方式对患者不利。

sentences.en: And what we found in the data that was striking is that the more experience the surgeon had, the less likely they were to change their behavior.
sentences.zh: 我们在数据中发现了一个惊人的事实：外科医生的经验越丰富，他们改变行为的可能性就越小。

sentences.en: That means that, as you were suggesting, when we gain experience often, we feel like the expert and we think that we know better,
sentences.zh: 这意味着，正如你所暗示的，当我们积累经验时，我们往往会觉得自己是专家，认为自己更懂，

sentences.en: even when we hear information or when we see evidence that speaks to the fact that we're wrong.
sentences.zh: 即使当我们听到信息或看到证据表明我们错了的时候也是如此。

sentences.en: And so having that learning mindset as we're gaining experience is so, so important.
sentences.zh: 因此，在积累经验的同时保持学习的心态是非常、非常重要的。

sentences.en: And of course, that's difficult to do precisely because once you know something, you ask yourself, why should I go back to becoming a beginner?
sentences.zh: 当然，这很难做到，正是因为一旦你懂了某些东西，你就会问自己：我为什么要回到初学者的状态？

sentences.en: You describe a very interesting study that was done out of Columbia University looking at guitar players and one way that expert guitarists could learn to once again think like beginners.
sentences.zh: 你描述了哥伦比亚大学进行的一项非常有趣的研究，观察吉他手，以及专家吉他手如何重新像初学者一样思考。

sentences.en: Tell me about that study.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说那项研究。

sentences.en: This is a study by Ting Zhang, and she was fascinated by this idea that once you're an expert, it's very difficult to look at problems with the eyes of a novice.
sentences.zh: 这是张婷（音译）的一项研究，她对一个想法很着迷：一旦你成为专家，就很难用新手的眼光看待问题。

sentences.en: And so one way she thought she could address this very issue
sentences.zh: 所以她认为解决这个问题的一个方法是，

sentences.en: is by asking expert to relive the experience of being a novice.
sentences.zh: 让专家重温作为新手的体验。

sentences.en: So in one of her studies, she recruited experienced people who play guitar.
sentences.zh: 在她的研究中，她招募了有经验的吉他手。

sentences.en: She asked some of them, the control group, to play as they would on a typical day.
sentences.zh: 她要求其中一些人（对照组）像往常一样演奏。

sentences.en: Of course, they sounded great.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们弹得很好。

sentences.en: She asked the others to play a song with their non-dominant hand.
sentences.zh: 她要求其他人用非惯用手弹奏一首歌。

sentences.en: Lefties played with the right hand.
sentences.zh: 左撇子用右手弹。

sentences.en: Right-handed people played with their left hand.
sentences.zh: 右撇子用左手弹。

sentences.en: It instantly made them feel like beginners again.
sentences.zh: 这让他们立刻感觉自己又成了初学者。

sentences.en: The experience is very humbling
sentences.zh: 这种体验非常令人谦卑，

sentences.en: because you're sort of reminded of what it is
sentences.zh: 因为你会被提醒，

sentences.en: that you knew and didn't know as you started.
sentences.zh: 在你刚开始时，你知道什么，又不知道什么。

sentences.en: And when she compared the advice
sentences.zh: 当她比较这些人给出的建议时，

sentences.en: that these people were giving to others
sentences.zh: 也就是给那些

sentences.en: who were interested in learning how to play the guitar,
sentences.zh: 有兴趣学习弹吉他的人的建议，

sentences.en: the advice was much more helpful
sentences.zh: 这些建议要有用得多，

sentences.en: when it came to this second group of people
sentences.zh: 当涉及到这第二组人时，

sentences.en: rather than the group of people who played the guitar
sentences.zh: 而不是那些像往常一样

sentences.en: as you would usually do.
sentences.zh: 弹吉他的那组人。

sentences.en: As I'm hearing you tell me about the guitar study,
sentences.zh: 当我听你讲这个吉他研究时，

sentences.en: it reminds me of something else you have in the book,
sentences.zh: 它让我想起了你书中的另一件事，

sentences.en: this insight that in many fields,
sentences.zh: 这个洞察是：在许多领域，

sentences.en: the people who are the innovators
sentences.zh: 那些创新者，

sentences.en: are often not the people who've been in those fields
sentences.zh: 往往不是那些在这些领域

sentences.en: for extended periods of time.
sentences.zh: 待了很长时间的人。

sentences.en: That it's often the newcomers to a field
sentences.zh: 往往是领域里的新人，

sentences.en: who have just about enough information
sentences.zh: 他们掌握了足够多的信息，

sentences.en: to have mastered the rules,
sentences.zh: 足以精通规则，

sentences.en: but I have not spent so much time in the culture that they've become hidebound.
sentences.zh: 但又没有在那种文化中待得太久，以至于变得墨守成规。

sentences.en: These are the people who are actually able to take the culture and move it in new directions.
sentences.zh: 这些人实际上能够引领文化并将其推向新的方向。

sentences.en: You talk about the role of how this works in science.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了这在科学领域是如何运作的。

sentences.en: There have been people who've tried to solve scientific problems
sentences.zh: 有些人试图解决科学问题，

sentences.en: by inviting people who are not necessarily science experts, but people who are outsiders.
sentences.zh: 通过邀请那些不一定是科学专家，而是外行的人。

sentences.en: It's quite interesting to think about the fact that probably all of us have had,
sentences.zh: 想到这一点非常有趣：我们所有人可能都曾，

sentences.en: at some point in our lives or another, a moment in which we were trying to tackle a problem
sentences.zh: 在生命中的某个时刻，遇到过试图解决某个问题的时候，

sentences.en: where we felt we were the expert, but we were stuck and we were not able to come up with a
sentences.zh: 我们觉得自己是专家，但却陷入了困境，无法想出

sentences.en: solution.
sentences.zh: 解决方案。

sentences.en: And what is interesting is that when we in fact bring in people who might not have the
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当我们实际上引入那些可能没有

sentences.en: right expertise, they're going to look at the problem from a very different perspective.
sentences.zh: 相关专业知识的人时，他们会从非常不同的角度看待问题。

sentences.en: And
sentences.zh: 而

sentences.en: that type of difference in perspective, in opinions, in the way you're looking and analyzing
sentences.zh: 这种在观点、看法以及观察和分析问题方式上的差异，

sentences.en: the problem can be quite powerful in helping you find a solution.
sentences.zh: 在帮助你找到解决方案时会非常强大。

sentences.en: And there are companies out there
sentences.zh: 现在确实有一些公司

sentences.en: that in fact have used this insight
sentences.zh: 利用了这个洞察。

sentences.en: and created businesses like Eli Lilly would be one of them
sentences.zh: 并创造了像礼来公司这样的企业，这只是其中之一

sentences.en: where when there are very difficult challenges,
sentences.zh: 在遇到非常困难的挑战时，

sentences.en: they put them out there such that
sentences.zh: 他们会把问题抛出来，这样

sentences.en: not only the people with the right expertise
sentences.zh: 不仅是那些拥有专业知识的人

sentences.en: might want to tackle the problem,
sentences.zh: 可能想要解决这个问题，

sentences.en: but all others, people who might not have the right expertise
sentences.zh: 而且其他人，那些可能没有相关专业知识的人

sentences.en: can chime in and often the solutions
sentences.zh: 也能参与进来，而解决方案往往

sentences.en: come exactly from those people.
sentences.zh: 正是来自这些人。

sentences.en: It's a good reminder that expertise
sentences.zh: 这很好地提醒了我们，专业知识

sentences.en: while wonderful, creates potential problems if we use it as a way of saying, I know the answer,
sentences.zh: 虽然很棒，但如果我们用它来作为一种借口，说“我知道答案，

sentences.en: I'm the expert.
sentences.zh: 我是专家”，就会产生潜在的问题。

sentences.en: You look at the problem tunarily, usually only from one perspective, and it's our
sentences.zh: 你通常只会从一个角度，也就是我们

sentences.en: own perspective.
sentences.zh: 自己的角度来看待问题。

sentences.en: And instead, having this learning mindset, bringing in novices into the problem
sentences.zh: 相反，保持这种学习心态，让新手参与到问题中来，

sentences.en: allows us to now look at the situation from many different angles and viewpoints.
sentences.zh: 让我们现在能够从许多不同的角度和观点来看待情况。

sentences.en: Of course, this speaks to the idea of the value of diversity.
sentences.zh: 当然，这谈到了多样性的价值这一理念。

sentences.en: I think that's one of the insights that I'm getting from what you just said.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我从你刚才所说的话中得到的见解之一。

sentences.en: Having a mix of people in the room who look at things from different perspectives could just be inherently valuable.
sentences.zh: 在房间里有一群从不同角度看问题的人，这本身可能就很有价值。

sentences.en: Having people who look at the problem from a very different perspective is, in fact, a key to solving tough probleMs.
sentences.zh: 事实上，拥有从非常不同的角度看待问题的人，是解决棘手问题的关键。

sentences.en: But the reality is that many of us don't want to be challenged.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，我们许多人并不想受到挑战。

sentences.en: It's so much easier to go through life, whether at work or at home for that matter, with people that just nod their heads and say, yep, I agree with you.
sentences.zh: 无论是在工作中还是在家里，与那些只会点头说“是的，我同意你”的人在一起，生活要容易得多。

sentences.en: But rebel leaders and rebel employees are people who really try to surround themselves with people who think differently and with people who do challenge them.
sentences.zh: 但叛逆的领导者和叛逆的员工，是那些真正试图让自己周围的人与众不同，并真正挑战他们的人。

sentences.en: I asked Francesca about another rebel she mentions in her book.
sentences.zh: 我问了弗朗西斯卡关于她在书中提到的另一位叛逆者。

sentences.en: You might be familiar with her work in movies such as Selma, an account of a series of famous civil rights marches led by Martin Luther King Jr.
sentences.zh: 你可能熟悉她在电影《塞尔玛》中的作品，这是一部讲述马丁·路德·金领导的一系列著名民权游行的影片，
发生在1965年。

sentences.en: That means proteSt. That means march.
sentences.zh: 那意味着抗议。那意味着游行。

sentences.en: That means disturb the peace.
sentences.zh: 那意味着扰乱治安。

sentences.en: That means jail.
sentences.zh: 那意味着坐牢。

sentences.en: And you say that her story reveals another really important idea when it comes to rebel talent,
sentences.zh: 你说她的故事揭示了关于叛逆天赋的另一个非常重要的观点，

sentences.en: which is the importance of being vigilant to stereotypes, to recognize that stereotypes can actually serve as a kind of straitjacket that prevents us from thinking creatively.
sentences.zh: 那就是对刻板印象保持警惕的重要性，要认识到刻板印象实际上可以成为一种束缚，阻止我们进行创造性思考。

sentences.en: In all sorts of spheres of life, we are affected by stereotypes, or more generally, we accept social roles that others have passed on to us.
sentences.zh: 在生活的各个领域，我们都受到刻板印象的影响，或者更广泛地说，我们接受了别人传给我们的社会角色。

sentences.en: And the story of Eva Duvernay is a beautiful one because she just doesn't do that.
sentences.zh: 艾娃·杜威内的故事很美，因为她根本不那样做。

sentences.en: And this comes from a person who decided to go to filmmaking later in her career.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个在职业生涯后期才决定从事电影制作的人。

sentences.en: She was doing a different job, and she said, I'm going to switch and enter this job.
sentences.zh: 她当时做着不同的工作，她说：“我要转行进入这个行业。”

sentences.en: And in the advice that she was receiving from others, everybody was talking about the importance of really being supported by others, reaching out to networks.
sentences.zh: 在从别人那里得到的建议中，每个人都在谈论真正得到他人支持、利用人脉的重要性。

sentences.en: She didn't have that.
sentences.zh: 她没有这些。

sentences.en: And she just started picking up the camera and working on her own movies.
sentences.zh: 她只是开始拿起摄像机，制作自己的电影。

sentences.en: And in fact, the first films she created were supported by her own savings.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她创作的第一批电影是由她自己的积蓄支持的。

sentences.en: And then she became known for the work that she was doing, for the fact that she was not accepting the rules of the business, but in a sense,
sentences.zh: 后来她因自己的作品而闻名，因为她不接受商业规则，但在某种意义上，

sentences.en: she was working and fighting against them.
sentences.zh: 她在工作并与这些规则抗争。

sentences.en: And it's quite amazing and inspiring as a story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常令人惊叹和鼓舞人心的故事。

sentences.en: And so for me, I made my first film, my first feature film when I was 38.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，我在38岁时制作了我的第一部电影，我的第一部故事片。

sentences.en: So it's never too late.
sentences.zh: 所以永远都不晚。

sentences.en: that I just started from the outside.
sentences.zh: 我只是从外部开始的。

sentences.en: We've seen how rebels constructively break the rules.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到了叛逆者是如何建设性地打破规则的。

sentences.en: They push ahead even when they don't have the support of power brokers.
sentences.zh: 即使在没有权力掮客支持的情况下，他们也会继续前进。

sentences.en: And once they achieve success, they continue to think like beginners
sentences.zh: 一旦他们取得成功，他们会继续像初学者一样思考，

sentences.en: and go out of their way to learn from those who disagree with them.
sentences.zh: 并特意向那些不同意他们的人学习。

sentences.en: So how can you activate your inner nonconformist?
sentences.zh: 那么，你如何激活你内心的不循规蹈矩者呢？

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续关注我们。

sentences.en: Today we're talking about rebels, people who break free of social norms
sentences.zh: 今天我们谈论的是叛逆者，那些打破社会规范

sentences.en: and achieve incredible feats of imagination.
sentences.zh: 并实现不可思议的想象力壮举的人。

sentences.en: Why is this something so few of us do?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们中很少有人这样做呢？

sentences.en: One problem is that we know too much.
sentences.zh: 一个问题是我们知道得太多了。

sentences.en: We become experts in our fields and then fall back on familiar routines.
sentences.zh: 我们成为了各自领域的专家，然后又回到了熟悉的常规中。

sentences.en: We forget how to see the world with fresh eyes.
sentences.zh: 我们忘记了如何用新鲜的眼光看待世界。

sentences.en: But it doesn't have to be this way.
sentences.zh: 但这不必如此。

sentences.en: Francesca Gino says that being a rebel is a skill that all of us can cultivate.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯卡·吉诺说，成为一名叛逆者是我们所有人都可以培养的一种技能。

sentences.en: Sometimes it takes only small steps.
sentences.zh: 有时只需要一小步。

sentences.en: A few years ago, she wondered if getting people to feel comfortable about being uncomfortable
sentences.zh: 几年前，她想知道让人们对“不舒服”感到自在，

sentences.en: could be the first step in activating their inner rebel.
sentences.zh: 是否能成为激活他们内心叛逆者的第一步。

sentences.en: She asked students to stand before their friends and classmates and sing
sentences.zh: 她让学生们站在朋友和同学面前唱歌，

sentences.en: Don't Stop Believing by Journey.
sentences.zh: 唱Journey乐队的《Don't Stop Believing》。

sentences.en: Can you set up the experiment for me, Francesca?
sentences.zh: 你能为我设置一下这个实验吗，弗朗西斯卡？

sentences.en: I'm putting my hand in my hair as I was reminded when I was running this study.
sentences.zh: 当我被提醒在进行这项研究时，我正把手放在头发上。

sentences.en: This was a study that was inspired by the notion that when we break rules, when we break away from what other people expect of us, we feel a sense of confidence.
sentences.zh: 这项研究的灵感来自于这样一个观念：当我们打破规则，当我们脱离别人对我们的期望时，我们会感到一种自信。

sentences.en: And so to test that, I brought undergraduates to the lab and I asked them to engage in the task that you just heard.
sentences.zh: 为了测试这一点，我把本科生带到实验室，让他们参与你刚才听到的任务。

sentences.en: Stand up in front of a video with a microphone and in front of other participants watching you singing Don't Stop Believing.
sentences.zh: 站在视频前，拿着麦克风，在其他参与者面前唱歌，唱《Don't Stop Believing》。

sentences.en: That was one of the songs.
sentences.zh: 那是其中一首歌。

sentences.en: And some of the participants did just that, but some others were asked to wear a bandana
sentences.zh: 一些参与者确实这样做了，但另一些人被要求戴上头巾

sentences.en: as they were singing, something that they told me made them uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 唱歌时，他们告诉我这让他们感到不舒服。

sentences.en: And then I was interested in seeing whether the anxiety and stress that they experienced
sentences.zh: 然后我有兴趣看看他们经历的焦虑和压力

sentences.en: during the task and their level of confidence, in addition to their performance, was going
sentences.zh: 在任务期间，以及他们的自信水平，除了他们的表现之外，是否会

sentences.en: to be different in these two different conditions.
sentences.zh: 在这两种不同的条件下有所不同。

sentences.en: And it was both looking at physiological measure of stress, but also their self-reported measures in answering the question of how confident they felt.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是观察压力的生理指标，也是他们在回答“他们感到多自信”这个问题时的自我报告指标。

sentences.en: People who were wearing the bandana while they were singing in front of their peers felt more confident, felt less stress.
sentences.zh: 在同伴面前唱歌时戴着头巾的人感到更自信，压力更小。

sentences.en: So despite the fact that they thought they would feel more uncomfortable and that it would be harder for them,
sentences.zh: 所以尽管他们认为自己会感到更不舒服，而且这对他们来说会更难，

sentences.en: The fact that they were wearing their bandana, something that the peers didn't expect, was actually helpful to them.
sentences.zh: 他们戴着头巾这一事实，即同伴们没想到的事情，实际上对他们有帮助。

sentences.en: And this is not just their feelings and their physiology.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是他们的感受和生理状况。

sentences.en: When you look at the performance in terms of how much they stay on tune, since the karaoke was recording that objectively, they did better.
sentences.zh: 当你从他们保持音准的程度来看表现时，因为卡拉OK客观地记录了这一点，他们做得更好。

sentences.en: So there's a paradox here, because in the one case, you're asking one set of students to sing the song, which is clearly difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一个悖论，因为在一种情况下，你要求一组学生唱这首歌，这显然很困难，

sentences.en: and especially before your friends in a classroom, it's difficult to do.
sentences.zh: 特别是在教室里的朋友面前，这很难做到。

sentences.en: But the second group is being asked to do something even more difficult.
sentences.zh: 但第二组被要求做一些更困难的事情。

sentences.en: You're asking them to sing the song and also wear this non-conforming, you know, headdress.
sentences.zh: 你要求他们唱这首歌，还要戴上这种不循规蹈矩的头饰。

sentences.en: And you would think that the second group would do worse, but you found exactly the opposite.
sentences.zh: 你会认为第二组会表现得更差，但你发现的恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Oftentimes we think that breaking rules is going to lead to worse outcomes
sentences.zh: 我们通常认为打破规则会导致更糟糕的结果，

sentences.en: and it's going to make us feel uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 而且会让我们感到不舒服。

sentences.en: And it does to a certain extent, but it then turns into confidence.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上确实如此，但随后它会转化为自信。

sentences.en: And that confidence translates in better performance.
sentences.zh: 而这种自信会转化为更好的表现。

sentences.en: It is paradoxical, but it's one of the big lessons in being rebelliousness.
sentences.zh: 这很矛盾，但这是叛逆行为带来的重大教训之一。

sentences.en: It does pay off.
sentences.zh: 它确实有回报。

sentences.en: I understand that you've discovered this about yourself as well.
sentences.zh: 我明白你也在这方面发现了自己的这一点。

sentences.en: You've run experiments of a sort where you try on the effects of different kinds of footwear
sentences.zh: 你进行过某种实验，尝试不同类型的鞋子带来的效果，

sentences.en: and the effects it has on your audiences.
sentences.zh: 以及它对你的听众产生的影响。

sentences.en: One time I was asked to teach two classes, the same class, back to back.
sentences.zh: 有一次我被要求连续教授两节课，同一门课。

sentences.en: And in each class I had 110 executives.
sentences.zh: 每节课我有110名高管。

sentences.en: And since I was teaching the same content across the two classes,
sentences.zh: 由于我在两节课中教授相同的内容，

sentences.en: what I thought I could do is change my shoes in between the two classes.
sentences.zh: 我想我可以做的是在两节课之间换鞋。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what I did.
sentences.zh: 这正是我的做法。

sentences.en: So picture this professor dressed up in a really nice suit.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下这位穿着非常漂亮西装的教授。

sentences.en: And for the first class, I was wearing formal leather shoes, probably what the students expected from an HBS professor or a professor in general teaching in exec ed.
sentences.zh: 第一节课，我穿着正式的皮鞋，这可能是学生们对哈佛商学院教授或一般在高管教育中授课的教授的期望。

sentences.en: But for the second class, I changed out my leather shoes for a pair of red sneakers.
sentences.zh: 但第二节课，我把皮鞋换成了一双红色的运动鞋。

sentences.en: And it was interesting to walk to class.
sentences.zh: 走进教室很有趣。

sentences.en: My colleagues were giving me the strange look, thinking what it is that she's doing.
sentences.zh: 我的同事们用奇怪的眼神看着我，心想她在做什么。

sentences.en: And I was going to teach my second class.
sentences.zh: 我正要去上我的第二节课。

sentences.en: And at the end of each of the two classes, I gave the executives a little survey.
sentences.zh: 在每节课结束时，我给高管们做了一个小调查。

sentences.en: And in the survey, I was asking them questions like, how much do you think I charge for my consulting?
sentences.zh: 在调查中，我问他们诸如“你认为我的咨询费是多少？”之类的问题，

sentences.en: How much influence do you think I have at HBS as a professor?
sentences.zh: “你认为我作为教授在哈佛商学院有多大的影响力？”

sentences.en: How often do you think I publish in a practitioner-oriented magazine like Harvard Business Review?
sentences.zh: “你认为我多久在《哈佛商业评论》这样的从业者导向杂志上发表文章？”

sentences.en: And what was interesting is that these are measures that capture how much influence the student thought I had.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，这些指标捕捉到了学生认为我有多大的影响力。

sentences.en: And what the survey results showed is that they had higher respect.
sentences.zh: 调查结果显示，他们有更高的尊重。

sentences.en: They thought of me as a more influential person when I taught them the same content, just wearing red sneakers.
sentences.zh: 当我教授同样的内容，只是穿着红色运动鞋时，他们认为我是一个更有影响力的人。

sentences.en: So, of course, people listening to this are going to go out and get red sneakers and wear
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，听到这个的人明天会出去买红色运动鞋并戴上

sentences.en: bandanas to work tomorrow, because that's what you're saying is going to get them taken more
sentences.zh: 头巾去上班，因为这就是你说会让别人更认真对待他们的原因。

sentences.en: seriously.
sentences.zh: 我最近为一家公司做了一次关于叛逆天赋问题的培训，邀请我去的那些人

sentences.en: I recently did a training for a company around the issues of rebel talent, and the people
sentences.zh: 都在团队中穿着红色运动鞋，他们整天都得到了很多赞美

sentences.en: who invited me out were all in a team wearing red sneakers, and they got a lot of compliments
sentences.zh: 和提问。

sentences.en: and questions throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这可能是从这项研究中学到的教训之一。

sentences.en: So, yes, that could be one of the lessons learned out of this research.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都能更好地打破规则的另一种方式

sentences.zh: 是保持对周围发生的事情的关注。

sentences.zh: 我经常在课堂上使用这段视频。

sentences.en: time to walk in and help.

sentences.zh: 他在两万名现场观众和数百万
